intro: Good evening, and welcome to the exhibit. Every day the dice roll a premise and a dozen constraints, and the game has to honour all of them. Today's roll was seed 1561779937. If you would follow me, each roll, and what the museum made of it.

rolls.value: a weather vane that can't decide · assembling · cupcakes
rolls.became: Why would a weathercock make cupcakes? Because every wind brings a different smell, and Wendell is hungry for all of them, which is exactly why he spins. A cupcake is the one food that needs every wind: flour from the windmill in the north, honey from the hives in the east, eggs from the henhouse in the south, cream from the dairy in the west. He assembles them from what the four winds bring.

rolls.value: trace a rune to cast it
rolls.became: A weather vane already has runes: the letters on its compass arms. You trace the one he has spun to (N, the old rune ᛖ for E, the lightning-bolt ᛊ for S, and W) and that wind blows its ingredient onto the bakery sill. Later, the Whirlwind: a circle, for when he can't decide at all.
Wendell is tin. He has never eaten anything. He wears a bib anyway (you can buy it), keeps a very small fork under his wing for later, and the placard counts every cupcake he has made and not eaten.

Every time a weathercock points, it points at somebody. A rooster pointing straight at you over a pile of cupcakes looks, to a pigeon, like an invitation. So the pigeons on whichever side he pointed at most come in to collect, and the guard breezes blow them back.
Oddwick, the village on the plinth, and Ottoline, Secretary of the Oddwick Pigeon Society, who signs her notes with a neat little O.

rolls.value: it turns out someone asked for it
rolls.became: The pigeons were never thieves. They were carrier pigeons, and their envelopes held an order: 9,999 cupcakes for the Grand Jubilee, leave on the sill. The scraps you can buy with feathers were pieces of it all along.
About half an hour, from the first rune to the last crumb, in one sitting.

rolls.value: workers you assign between jobs · auto-battle waves of enemies
rolls.became: First the breezes: little puff-cheeked winds who work for cupcakes, shuffled between the mill, the hives, the hens, the churn and guard duty. A cupcake needs one of each ingredient, so the slowest job sets the pace. Then the pigeons: waves that fly in by themselves from the side you pointed at most, fought off by the guards without you lifting a finger (though a rune traced toward their side helps). Pigeons that are blown back leave feathers, which buy the battle its own upgrades.

Farms really do help each other. The empty plots between the farms grow sunflowers (bees love them, the seeds go in the flour), clover (bees and hens), a haystack (hens nest in it, cows eat it) and a mill pond (cows drink, the wheel turns). Each one boosts the two farms beside it; the dotted paths on the diorama show where.

rolls.value: the number hits its cap and the world crunches
rolls.became: The placard counter was installed in 1974 with four digits. At 9,999 it cannot go any higher, the plinth cannot hold another crumb, and the diorama crunches into one cupcake the size of a village, with Wendell on top like a cake topper.
Cupcakes, counted one by one on a four-digit placard. The whole game is one placard's worth.
A model village on a plinth in a museum after hours, at 1:48 scale, drawn in isometric under one gallery spotlight, with a brass label and a counter on the front.
Eight colours of a gallery at night: navy dark, cream labels, brass trim, dusty rose and mauve for the roofs, and slate for the pigeons.

Gallery jazz: a walking bass and brushes, with vibes joining when the pigeons do. The whole-tone scale has no home key, so the tune never quite settles. Neither does Wendell. When the pigeons arrive it shifts up a semitone, into the only other whole-tone scale there is.
Every log line is a stop on the tour, read in the hushed, slightly worried voice of a guide who is increasingly sure the exhibit is moving.
No calendar nod today. The exhibit is timeless; only the pigeons are on a schedule.

outro: This concludes the tour. Please do not feed the pigeons. Please do not feed the weathercock either. He is tin, and he is saving himself.
